findings.title: website_name bypasses TL0 anonymous field hiding
findings.body: website_name is derived from website but is not covered by untrusted_attributes, and website_name never calls scope.restrict_user_fields?. For a TL0 user seen anonymously, include_website? is forced false so website is omitted, yet website_name is still serialized. The profile template renders the globe label from model.website_name, so anonymous viewers get the host and, when the heuristic matches, the path of a field this serializer intentionally hides to limit new-user spam. Add website_name to untrusted_attributes (or apply the same guard in include_website_name?) and extend the existing TL0 anonymous serializer example; the new specs only cover a normal user.

findings.title: include_website_name is never invoked
findings.body: ActiveModel::Serializer only calls inclusion hooks named include_<attr>?, and every other hook in this file follows that form. include_website_name has no question mark, so it is dead code and website_name is always emitted, including null when the user has no website. Rename it to include_website_name?. As written it only checks website.present?, so renaming alone does not apply the TL0 restriction.

findings.title: Same-domain check misclassifies hosts
findings.body: The non-equal branches do not test whether the website is actually on the instance domain, so the profile label either appends a path for an unrelated site or drops it for the same site. The elsif treats hosts as the same domain when they have the same label count greater than 2 and share every label except the first, which matches community.co.uk with paypal.co.uk and foo.github.io with bar.github.io and then appends the path. The else branch uses discourse_host.ends_with?("." + website_host), which is true for any suffix, so a website host of com or co.uk matches every forum on that suffix. The common www case fails the other way: a forum on example.com and a website of http://www.example.com/docs has a different label count and example.com does not end with .www.example.com, so only the host is shown. Comparison is also case-sensitive against Discourse.current_hostname while URI#host is lowercased, so a mixed-case hostname misses the exact-match branch. The new specs only cover example.com vs discourse.org, an exact match, and a parent forums.example.com, so they do not catch this. Compare normalized registrable domains (and an optional www label) instead of stripping one label or using a raw suffix check.
